D: Architecture and end-to-end flow (dat.lens: D: Architecture and end-to-end flow (data in -> events -> folding -> nightly -> sweep/triggers -> dispatch -> events back -> learning -> proof -> UI), checked against what AUTONOMY_V3=1 actually reaches in production
D: Architecture and end-to-end flow (dat.summary: AUTONOMY_V3=1 is wired, but only partly. It reaches build_runtime, the worker and the API runtime through settings.py:886-892 and v3.py. On the live decision path it switches on 7 pieces: the profile, look-alike, who, moments, journeys, frequency and offer pricing. It also adds an experiments wrapper that has nothing to run, because nothing in production starts an experiment. Five of the headline v3 items exist only as a library, tests and a Gym policy: live experiments, AI copy with its scoring model, generated images with batch approval, early signals with auto-budget, and the whole-budget rebalance. The UI only got mock JSON. Several pieces that are wired break against real data or a real deployment. Offer redemptions are never charged to the budget when orders come from Shopify, because discount codes are not offer ids; the Gym hides this by writing the agent's own offer_id onto purchases. Everything v3 learns lives in process memory and is thrown away whenever a goal's policy is rebuilt: on every restart or deploy, every content approval, and every change to a brief's envelope (budget, caps, channels or offers). The who book keeps every event of every customer as a Python object for each goal, about 1.7 KB per event as measured. That makes AUTONOMY_V3 an out-of-memory risk even for an 8k-customer shop with Klaviyo history, and unusable at 300k customers. The Data Doctor's new order-log path builds a v1 AutoML table and has no link to the agent's event store. The CSV-to-events route returns the events and never stores them, so only a Shopify or Klaviyo connection can feed the agent. Running the system means one worker process (it is not safe to run several), at least 46 environment settings plus about 68 v3 settings that can only be changed in code, and one all-or-nothing switch. None of it has been measured against the v2 agent or the best simple rule. Some things are sound: per-customer failures are isolated, the slow models turn themselves off on noise or thin data, and journeys are rebuilt from the decision log after a restart.
sound: Each customer's decision is isolated from failures: if the policy raises, that customer is logged as DO_NOTHING with probability 1 and the goal gets an alert counting the failures (service.py:1993-2032), so one bad customer cannot stop the sweep. Profile building and learning are wrapped the same way (service.py:2730, 2858, 2949).

The slow models (leaving risk, 90-day value) fail safe. On random synthetic data with 300 and 1,200 customers they refused themselves (AUC 0.51 against a 0.60 bar; value skill -4% against a +5% bar). With 0, 3 or 40 customers WhoBook.refresh does not raise and reports 'not used' (probe tiny.py). A weak model does not quietly steer bids.
The profile groups order lines into orders by attrs order_id or invoice_no (profile/facts.py:15, 315), so a Shopify order with many lines is not counted as many orders.
A rebuilt policy replays journey runs from the decision log (agent.py:2717-2722), so a restart does not send a second first message to a customer halfway through a journey.

The job queue claims with SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (store/queue.py:66), and the day's decisions are reloaded on restart (_start_day), so the same customer and goal is not decided twice on one day.

The preset is off by default, and a fingerprint test pins the default v2 agent's decisions as unchanged. The docs (PRESET.md 'What the preset does not fix', LOOKALIKE.md:72-77, IMAGES.md:156+) admit openly that many of the gaps below exist. The problem is the way STATUS.md presents them under 'Built'.

findings.assumption: Offer pricing and the whole-budget planner keep offer spend to the goal's budget, because each redemption is charged to the goal that sent the offer.
findings.problem: A redemption is charged only when the purchase's attrs.offer_id exactly equals the envelope's OfferOption.offer_id (e.g. 'pct10'). The Shopify connector fills offer_id with the first discount code typed at checkout (e.g. 'COMEBACK10'). OfferOption has no discount-code field, nothing maps codes to offers, and nothing in the runtime ever calls the connector's CREATE_DISCOUNT write. In production the BudgetPrice therefore sees channel spend only, offer spend reads as zero, and the price falls toward 0, so the budget never limits offers. The Gym passes only because its simulator writes the agent's own offer_id and offer_cost onto purchases.
findings.evidence: agent.py:2860 stores _offer_goal[(customer, d.action.offer_id)]; agent.py:2868 looks it up with e.attrs['offer_id']. connectors/shopify/mapping.py:151 sets 'offer_id': codes[0]. gym/world.py:523 and 679 write {'offer_id': a.offer_id, 'offer_cost': ...}. Probe redeem.py: offer_id='pct10' -> 6.0 charged; 'COMEBACK10' -> 0.0; 'MAI-7F3K2Q' -> 0.0. grep for CREATE_DISCOUNT outside connectors/tests: no caller.
findings.real_world_impact: Take the 8k Shopify brand running 10%-off codes. The offer price stays at 0, so every offer is costed at face value with no budget pressure. Discount spend can run past the goal's budget until the mandate's separate money rule stops it, if that rule counts redemptions at all. The 'whole-budget planner' claim does not hold on real orders.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit code-to-offer mapping: a code or code_prefix on OfferOption, or generate per-send codes with CREATE_DISCOUNT and record code -> decision. Add a test that feeds a Shopify-mapped order through the real mapping into _price_redemption. Until then, do not claim offer budget control.

findings.assumption: v3's learned state (look-alike crowd, sleeping-dog verdicts, offer price, experiments, tiredness rows) builds up over time in production.
findings.problem: All of it lives in the per-goal policy object. The runtime builds a new policy whenever the cache key changes. The key is (material_brief, approved content ids), and material_brief includes the whole envelope: budget, channels, offers, caps, holdout. A restart, a deploy, approving or retiring any content item, the weekly strategist narrowing an envelope, or a human changing the budget therefore all wipe it. After a rebuild: the look-alike crowd starts empty (the replay does not reach it, as LOOKALIKE.md:72-77 admits); WhoBook._frozen is empty, so customers held back as sleeping dogs now have low recent load and are keyed into the light-contact group again, which is exactly the oscillation the docstring at who.py:342-346 says freezing exists to prevent; BudgetPrice is re-created with the whole budget and a fresh 30-day plan, forgetting what was spent (agent.py:2838); the ExperimentBook is empty (v3.py:121). test_the_offer_price_follows_a_budget_that_moves... passes the new brief to the same in-memory agent, a path the runtime never takes, so the 'keeps its spend' claim has no test on the production path.
findings.evidence: service.py:3044-3054 (key and rebuild); MATERIAL_BRIEF_FIELDS service.py:303-305 include 'envelope'; agent.py:2836-2838; who.py:342-346 and 404-414; v3.py:118-121; tests/v3/preset/test_preset.py:451-460; PRESET.md 'The experiment book is not persisted'.
findings.real_world_impact: A team that deploys weekly and approves new creative every week never has more than a few days of v3 learning, and the offer budget restarts on every deploy. Sleeping dogs the agent learned to leave alone get messaged again after each restart, which costs unsubscribes on a WhatsApp number with a quality rating.
findings.recommendation: Persist v3 state outside the process (look-alike rows and outcomes, frozen keys, BudgetPrice spend to date, ExperimentBook.snapshot) and restore it when a policy is built. Alternatively, make content approval and budget-only brief changes update the policy in place instead of rebuilding it. Add a runtime-level test: restart, then check that state is preserved.

findings.assumption: AUTONOMY_V3 suits 'pilots and small to mid-size shops'. Sweep batches of 5,000 keep memory bounded.
findings.problem: WhoBook.ingest keeps every event handed over as a pydantic Event in a dict, per goal, with no type filter. _feed_history passes every customer's whole history to every newly built policy (service.py:2807-2857), and a Klaviyo connection imports Received/Opened/Clicked email events for every past campaign. A measured Event costs about 1,685 bytes. sweep_batch bounds the sweep, but the who book still holds the whole log. On top of that, the slow models are fitted inside the first decision of a sweep (agent.py:2068 who.refresh in _decide), not in the nightly job. That fit is measured at about 1 ms per light customer (1,200 customers and 27k events: 1.1 s to build the training set plus 1.2 s to fit) and is repeated per goal. The worker's drain loop runs jobs one at a time, so a long tick also holds back send jobs, cart triggers, webhooks and connector syncs.
findings.evidence: who.py:334 (events dict) and 351-358 (ingest keeps all); service.py:2807-2857; agent.py:2716 and 2068; probe mem.py: 'bytes/event 1685.5'; probe slow.py: 300 customers -> build 0.25 s, fit 0.25 s; 1,200 customers -> 1.11 s and 1.18 s; worker.py:579-586 sequential drain.
findings.real_world_impact: 8k-customer brand, 14 months of orders, about 2 emails a week through Klaviyo: roughly 8k x ~250 events = 2M events, about 3.4 GB per goal; three goals come to about 10 GB in the worker, and the same again in the API process if it ticks. 300k-customer shop with 3 years: tens of millions of events, far past any normal container. The worker crashes out of memory, and on restart it re-feeds the full history, so it loops.
findings.recommendation: Do not let the who book hold raw events. Use the nightly profile (already on state) plus a compact per-customer digest, and move the slow-model and trait fits into the nightly job, streamed from SQL. Until that is done, gate AUTONOMY_V3 on a customer and event count and refuse to start above it.

findings.assumption: v3 as listed in STATUS.md 'Built' (experiments, copy, images, early signals, auto-budget, whole-budget planner) is part of the product when AUTONOMY_V3=1.
findings.problem: Five headline items cannot be reached from the production path. (1) Experiments: the preset wraps decide with an empty ExperimentBook, and nothing outside experiments/gymrun.py:228 calls book.start. There is no API, UI, persistence or weekly review (EXPERIMENTS.md:320 'Not wired into the runtime'). (2) Copy per customer type, its scoring model and live elimination: nothing imports autonomy.content. (3) Images: nothing constructs ImageServices, so the /v2/images routes return 503. The provider and vision checker are fakes, and the '95% caught' figure is 100% by construction because the fake checker reads flags the fake provider wrote (IMAGES.md:156-170). The output is SVG, which email clients do not show. The queue is in memory. (4) Early signals and auto-budget: no job calls them (PRESET.md 'Not switched on'). (5) The UI: v3 commits touched only ui/v2/mock/*.json; no screen shows image batches, experiments, journeys or who scores.
findings.evidence: grep 'from autonomy.content|import autonomy.content' outside the package: no results. grep 'ImageServices(' outside api/v2/images.py: no results. api/v2/app.py:124 attaches it only when the 'images' argument is passed. gymrun.py:228 is the only book.start. `git log -- ui/` for v3 commits shows mocks only (54329963, 7f487e17, d7964c4e, 86933894).
findings.real_world_impact: A buyer or the owner who reads plan-v3 or STATUS will think the agent runs its own experiments and writes copy and images per customer type. With AUTONOMY_V3=1 it does none of these. The marketer with 30 minutes a week has no screen to approve images or read a test.
findings.recommendation: Split STATUS.md into 'reachable in production with AUTONOMY_V3=1' and 'library only'. Count only the first as shipped. Wire experiments start, persist and review, and a UI, before claiming them as features.

findings.assumption: Phase 0's order-log path in the Data Doctor gives shops without connectors a way to feed the agent.
findings.problem: The order-log path builds a v1 AutoML training table (one row per lapsed shopper per month-end) inside engine/doctor. It has no link to autonomy's EventStore (ORDER_LOG.md:1-30; no autonomy import in engine/doctor/order_log*.py). The v2 CSV route POST /v2/engines/doctor/map-events maps a file to events and returns them in the response without storing them. autonomy/bridges/doctor_bridge.map_file has no caller outside tests. The only routes into the agent's event store are the Shopify/Klaviyo connectors and channel webhooks (deps.make_ingest). That leaves two separate pipelines that disagree: v1's order-log roll-up nets returns and drops guests; autonomy's EventMapping and connector mapping have their own rules.
findings.evidence: api/v2/engines/doctor.py:1386-1430 (returns MapEventsResponse(events=...), no append); grep 'doctor_bridge|map_file(' outside tests -> only its definition (doctor_bridge.py:75); api/v2/deps.py:640-652 ingest used only by receive_webhook (deps.py:466-486).
findings.real_world_impact: An Indian D2C shop on WooCommerce, Magento or a custom stack, or one that will only hand over a CSV export, can run the Data Doctor but can never start the agent. The 'India first' market is not Shopify-only.
findings.recommendation: Add an import job that writes mapped events from an upload or the order-log path into the EventStore with stable ids, then requests a rebuild. Make one mapping (returns, guests, order roll-up) the source of truth for both v1 and the agent.

findings.assumption: The runtime runs as several worker processes plus an API process, with each tick handled once.
findings.problem: Any worker can claim a tick job. tick_handler queues the next tick (5 minutes by default) before the current tick runs. There is no tick lease or runtime lock, so a tick that runs longer than 5 minutes (a v3 rebuild, history feed or slow-model fit; see D3) can overlap with a second worker's tick. Each process holds its own policies and v3 state, so ticks that alternate between processes split what is learned (two look-alike crowds, two offer prices, two frozen sets). build_worker creates RuntimeCursor() fresh, so a restart reruns the nightly and weekly jobs. The production API builds a second full runtime with the same v3 settings (api/v2/app.py:202), and POST /v2/runtime/tick decides with that separate, cold brain. No document says 'run exactly one worker'.
findings.evidence: worker.py:266-272 (successor queued before tick(now)); settings.py:155 tick_every_minutes=5; store/queue.py:55-80 (no reclaim or lease for RUNNING ticks); service.py:3313-3318 (no cursor passed); service.py:428-432 RuntimeCursor 'a worker can save it' but none does; api/v2/app.py:202; api/v2/routes.py:411-415.
findings.real_world_impact: A CRM team at a 300k-customer shop scales workers to 2 for throughput. Decisions then come from two inconsistent brains, budget pacing per process is off by up to 2x, and an operator tick from the API can send on top of the worker's sweep.
findings.recommendation: Use a database lease (advisory lock) per business for tick jobs. Persist RuntimeCursor. Make the API runtime read-only (no policies) or forbid operator ticks when a worker is running. Document a single tick owner.

findings.assumption: Profile features built from the shop's own Klaviyo engagement describe real customer behaviour.
findings.problem: Klaviyo's Opened Email and Clicked Email events map straight to OPEN and CLICK (klaviyo/mapping.py:56-59). Nothing filters Apple Mail Privacy Protection opens or bot or security-scanner clicks (grep for bot/apple/mpp/prefetch in profile and klaviyo: no results). They feed ch_open_rate, ch_click_rate, ch_engaged and ch_email_engage_rate. Who's trait groups split customers at the median click rate of 'engaged' customers (who.py:404-406), and the look-alike and tiredness models read the same profile.
findings.evidence: autonomy/connectors/klaviyo/mapping.py:56-59; profile features list (ch_open_rate, ch_click_rate, ch_engaged ...); who.py:404-406.
findings.real_world_impact: In India, iOS share is low but corporate mail scanners click links. In the US or EU, about 50% of opens are machine opens. Sleeping-dog trait groups and look-alikes get keyed partly on mail-client noise. The 'engaged' and 'click-rate' traits mean something different from what the Gym planted.
findings.recommendation: Mark machine opens (Klaviyo exposes an Apple privacy flag), drop clicks within a few seconds of delivery or from known scanner user agents, and build engagement features from clicks plus site visits rather than opens.

findings.assumption: The shipped journeys and calendar are sensible defaults for an India-first shop.
findings.problem: Journeys C and D are labelled 'WhatsApp now, high value only' with value_bar: 50 in the shop's currency (journeys.py:242, 443). For a rupee shop that is ₹50, which almost any order clears, so WhatsApp-first journeys are offered to nearly everyone. with_value_bar has no caller, so a shop cannot change it without editing the YAML. The India calendar holds only 2026-2027 festival dates (calendar_in.yaml:17), and from 2028 festival moments quietly disappear.
findings.evidence: configs/v3/journeys.yaml:38 and 44 'value_bar: 50'; autonomy/decide/journeys.py:443 compares first.value_if_converted < journey.value_bar; grep with_value_bar -> definition only; configs/v3/calendar_in.yaml:17 'The years listed are 2026 and 2027'.
findings.real_world_impact: Every WhatsApp marketing conversation is paid, and Meta penalises a number for blocks and low-quality template sends. A ₹50 bar turns a 'high value only' channel into the default and raises cost and block risk for the 8k brand.
findings.recommendation: Express value bars relative to the shop (e.g. top-quartile expected value, or a multiple of WhatsApp conversation cost), set them at onboarding, and alert when the calendar has no dates for the coming 90 days.

findings.assumption: Stacking 7 interacting parts on the v2 agent is a sensible next step and can be operated by a small team.
findings.problem: v3 adds about 13k lines and 663 tests in about 16 modules. It has about 68 settings that exist only in code (LookalikeConfig 17, WhoConfig 12, CopyConfig 22, ImageConfig 9, OfferPricing 6, FrequencyConfig 2), on top of 46 environment settings and 30 RuntimeConfig fields, behind one all-or-nothing switch. In production a part cannot be turned off alone: only lookalike_model and v3 are settings, and AUTONOMY_LOOKALIKE_MODEL=false is silently ignored when v3 is on (settings.py:386, v3.py resolve). The base agent never beat the best simple rule on randomised real data and overestimated value about 10x (REAL_DATA_RESULTS). v3 multiplies those same value estimates by urgency of up to 3.75x (moments 2.5 x who 1.5), and several pairs in PRESET.md are marked 'an approximation'. STATUS.md 'Not proven yet': no Gym or real-bench comparison has been run. The 'explain' engine (api/v2/engines/decisions.py:486) builds a plain v2 agent, so 'what would you do for this customer' disagrees with what live v3 does.
findings.evidence: Probe: RuntimeSettings 46 fields, RuntimeConfig 30, v3 configs 68; wc of v3 modules 12,989 lines; settings.py:384-388; docs/v3/STATUS.md 'Nothing here shows yet that v3 beats the plain agent or the best simple rule'; PRESET.md urgency row 'at most 3.75'.
findings.real_world_impact: If v3 underperforms in a pilot, the team cannot tell which part caused it or switch that part off without a code deploy. The marketer gets explanations that do not match what was sent. A 10x-overconfident value estimate times 3.75 is the risky direction for message volume and discounts.
findings.recommendation: Ship parts behind separate environment flags and turn them on one at a time against the simple-rule baseline. Have the explain endpoint use the live policy's configuration. Fix calibration (expected vs measured value) before any multiplier is allowed above 1.

findings.assumption: Sleeping dogs judged by traits protect a customer across the business.
findings.problem: There is one WhoBook per goal policy. Each goal fits its own trait groups on its own records and keeps its own _frozen set, so a customer goal A has learned to leave alone can still be contacted by goal B (one_contact_per_tick limits only a single tick). Splitting the records across goals also thins each fit.
findings.evidence: agent.py:1673-1675 who per AgentPolicy; service.py:3045-3054 one policy per goal_id; who.py:404-414 fit on harm.own_records() of that goal's bundle.
findings.real_world_impact: A shop running win-back, repeat-purchase and cart goals at once gets three independent and weaker sleeping-dog judgements.
findings.recommendation: Make the who book (and the contact-harm model it reads) business-wide and shared across goal policies.

findings.assumption: Look-alike learning has something to warm-start from on a real shop's history.
findings.problem: The look-alike warm start uses only past campaigns that had a randomised control (randomised_arms in _warm_lookalike). Ordinary Klaviyo campaign history has no holdout, so on a new shop and after every rebuild (D2) the look-alike model is exactly the click model until 150 treated and 60 control outcome windows of 7 days have closed again.
findings.evidence: agent.py:2353-2400 (_warm_lookalike requires arms with control); lookalike.py LookalikeConfig min_treated=150, min_control=60; DEFAULT_LEARN_HORIZON_DAYS=7 (agent.py:204); LOOKALIKE.md:72-77.
findings.real_world_impact: For the 8k brand, look-alike adds nothing for at least the first one to two weeks after each deploy or content change. In the Gym, which runs one long uninterrupted process, this cost never shows.
findings.recommendation: Count the agent's own holdout decisions replayed from the decision log as control rows on rebuild, which needs the persistence in D2, and report in the briefing whether look-alike is active.

C: AI / LLM loops and hallucination risk.lens: C: AI / LLM loops and hallucination risk
C: AI / LLM loops and hallucination risk.summary: The per-customer decision really is LLM-free, and most LLM roles are well boxed in by typed answers and code fallbacks. The Strategist and Scientist choose from enums, the Analyst falls back to a code-written template, and the Data Doctor has consent, per-case spend caps and masking. The main problem is not the box itself. Most of the LLM loops the plan describes are either not wired into the production build or not proven. The production app builds no LLM client for the marketing agent: brand copy, judge, Strategist, Analyst and reply classifier are all None or template. So a real shop gets about 20 fixed template sentences, approved on the rules alone. Where an LLM is plugged in, the code-side checks are weaker than the docs suggest. The zero-touch library sets judge_optional=True and uses the same model for writer and judge, so a judge outage auto-approves LLM copy. The Critic's rules miss 'flat 500 off', 'half price', BOGO, Hindi discounts, invented scarcity and made-up review counts. The Analyst's number check ignores the sign, so a loss can be reported as a gain and passes. The Data Doctor's grounding is lexical: '12% churn' is grounded by any 0.12 anywhere. The v3 per-type copy feature has a concrete hallucination generator built in code. In a typical D2C base, where more than two-thirds of customers bought once, every type is labelled 'repeat buyer', and that label is the only thing the writer sees. At the 8k-customer target its live test and scoring model can never reach their own thresholds, so raw LLM copy would go live: the exact failure the plan cites as the reason for the scoring model. WhatsApp per-type copy has no template-submission path, and the volume is far above what Meta allows. On the meta-risk: v3 STATUS lists items as 'Built' that nothing calls (copy planner, experiments start, image sending, auto-budget, the order-log tool). plan-v3 claims a reliability layer and a cross-family judge that the code does not have. No real-model eval of the Critic, Creative, copy-per-type or vision checker exists in the repo; only ScriptedLLM and fake-observer tests do. The only real-model evidence is the Scientist roles: recorded Sonnet answers in which code caught an invented p=0.048 and the Judge matched the code rule 4 of 4 times.
sound: The per-customer decision has no LLM in it (autonomy/runtime/service.py:88; the policy is maths). LLMs never set per-customer offers or probabilities.

Strategist and Scientist roles answer only in typed enums and bounded numbers. A bad answer is rejected, not patched, and a rule-based fallback is used (autonomy/agents/strategist.py:1-30, autonomy/agents/scientist_roles.py:1-40). The pick is made by a pre-registered evidence rule that the Judge can only veto. In recorded real Sonnet runs, code refused an invented p=0.048 and the Judge equalled the rule 4 of 4 times (docs/v2/SCIENTIST.md:118-127).
The Analyst always has a code-written template briefing to fall back on. An unreachable model never blocks a briefing (autonomy/agents/analyst.py:700-745).
The Critic fails closed by default: with judge_optional=False, a judge outage holds copy as DRAFT (autonomy/agents/critic.py:492-510). Rule failures never reach the judge.

In the Conversation agent the English STOP/complaint keyword net runs before any classifier, and a classifier failure goes to a person (autonomy/agents/conversation.py:170-200). LLMTextSignals JSON-encodes replies, validates labels in code and maps slips to the catch-all label (autonomy/signals/llm_signals.py).

Data Doctor AI: client consent is required before any call, plus per-case caps of 2M tokens and 200 calls and 8 chat steps per message (configs/engine.yaml:385-387; engine/doctor/ai_guard.py). Every file goes through an egress gate. Column names and cells are cleaned of hidden characters (engine/agent/untrusted.py). Outcome, consent, ID and date questions can only be answered by the person (engine/doctor/agent_chat.py _MEANING_TOPICS).

Images: prices and offer text are drawn by code with Decimal arithmetic, never by the model. The fake checker fails closed on images it cannot read (autonomy/assets/check.py:252-267). IMAGES.md and COPY.md honestly state that their evidence is synthetic or fake.

LLM cost is bounded, not runaway. Copy is capped at max_types x drafts (2,400 writes per goal-week, about 1,200 Creative calls plus 4,800 judge calls, up to 2x with JSON retries). Chat and Data Doctor cases have hard caps, and replies are batched 20 per call.

findings.assumption: v2/v3 is an AI marketing agent: 'AI writes per customer type', a Strategist and Analyst run the weekly loop, an LLM reads customer replies, and an LLM judge checks every message.
findings.problem: The production build constructs no LLM client for the marketing agent. BrandServices is built without llm, so goal_library uses _NoModel. Every Creative call raises, so every cell gets TEMPLATE_COPY, and with judge_optional=True the Critic approves it on rules alone. The Strategist is the keyword template_strategist. build_runtime gets analyst=None and strategist=None, so the weekly LLM cycle never runs. text_signals is None, so replies go to PersonReadsReplies. The Studio judge is None by default. The only live LLM in production is the v1 Data Doctor. Every LLM behaviour of the agents is exercised only through ScriptedLLM in tests and the demo.
findings.evidence: api/v2/app.py:153 and 163-166 (BrandServices built with no llm); autonomy/brand/samples.py:95-99 (_NoModel raises LLM_UNAVAILABLE) and 264-271 (judge_optional True, same model for Creative and Critic); api/v2/deps.py:715 and 1365 (strategist=template_strategist); autonomy/runtime/settings.py:774-775 and 900-902 (text_signals and analyst default None; strategist is not passed by api/v2/app.py:202); autonomy/runtime/service.py:1165 (PersonReadsReplies); api/v2/engines/studio.py:551-553 (get_judge_llm returns None). grep for RuntimeSettings LLM settings in autonomy/runtime/settings.py and api/v2/app.py found none.
findings.real_world_impact: The 8k-customer D2C shop gets about 2 fixed sentences per theme (the same ones every other client gets), labelled by theme for the bandit. The marketer is told an 'AI' writes and reviews copy and that a weekly AI plan adjusts; neither happens. The 300k shop's CRM team sees identical template copy across all goals. Any lift result therefore says nothing about the LLM pieces.
findings.recommendation: State plainly in STATUS and the pitch which LLM roles are live in the production build (today: only the Data Doctor). Add an explicit, tested settings path (env plus client builder) for the Creative, the judge (a separate model) and the reply classifier before claiming AI copy. Until then, describe the product as 'rule-checked template copy'.

findings.assumption: 'Nothing is approved without the judge' and 'the Critic gate on everything a customer sees', with 'a judge from a different model family' (plan-v3.md:277, 345; critic.py docstring).
findings.problem: The zero-touch library path sets judge_optional=True and passes the same model and model_id to both the Creative and the Critic. If an LLM is configured and the judge call fails (rate limit, timeout, outage), the first failure marks the judge down for the rest of the review. Every remaining LLM-written draft is then APPROVED on the deterministic rules alone. Those rules catch discounts only when written with % or 'percent' or a currency marker. They miss 'flat 500 off', 'half price', 'buy 1 get 1 free', 'upto 70 off', '50 प्रतिशत छूट', invented deadlines ('sale ends tonight', 'only 3 left') and invented social proof ('10,000 happy customers', 'Rated 4.9').
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Marketing-ai-/b3510c52-036a-5471-a52e-fd5d81ce4bd7/scratchpad/redteam/critic_probe.py: check_rules returned [] for 7 of 8 dishonest bodies (only 'Rs. 500 off' was caught). With a judge that raises LLMError and judge_optional=True, all 7 came back 'approved on the rules alone (judge optional)'. Code: autonomy/brand/samples.py:266-271; autonomy/agents/critic.py:127-128 (_PERCENT, _MONEY_BEFORE), 454 (down latch), 504-507 (judge_optional approves).
findings.real_world_impact: A Diwali week rate-limit means the Indian shop's WhatsApp and email library goes out with an invented 'flat ₹500 off' the shop never approved, or a fake 'ends tonight'. That brings refund disputes, consumer-protection exposure, and WhatsApp quality-rating hits that cannot be undone (DECISIONS V-1). The same-model judge also defeats the self-grading protection the plan relies on.
findings.recommendation: Never use judge_optional for LLM-written copy; restrict it to TEMPLATE_COPY. Require a judge client distinct from the writer, and refuse to construct if it is the same model. Make a judge outage hold drafts, not approve them. Extend the rules: any digit run near off/discount/flat/upto/free, BOGO and half-price patterns, Hindi and Hinglish discount words, and deadline and scarcity phrases ('tonight', 'only N left', 'ends', 'last day') unless the brief carries a real end date.

findings.assumption: Customer types get 'plain labels' that are 'all the writer is told about the type' (COPY.md section 1), so per-type copy is accurate.
findings.problem: Labels use terciles of the base. When more than two-thirds of customers have 1 purchase (normal for D2C), q_lo == q_hi, and _tercile_word returns the middle word 'repeat buyer' for every type, one-time buyers included. The LLM is then told the reader is a repeat buyer and will write 'thanks for coming back' copy. The Critic's judge never sees the type label, so it cannot catch the false personal claim. Labels are also relative to the shop's own distribution: 'frequent buyer' can mean 2 orders.
findings.evidence: autonomy/content/types.py:316-318 (if low >= high: return words[1]) and 357-361. Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Marketing-ai-/b3510c52-036a-5471-a52e-fd5d81ce4bd7/scratchpad/redteam/types_probe.py on 1,500 synthetic customers (70% one order) gave 75 types and 'one-time buyers in repeat/frequent-labelled types': 1047 of 1047. ct000 'lapsed, repeat buyer, mid spend…' has 89 members, all with exactly 1 purchase. autonomy/agents/critic.py:_judge_prompt has no type label.
findings.real_world_impact: For the 8k Shopify shop, which is mostly one-time buyers, every per-type draft would address one-time buyers as loyal regulars, and that would happen in thousands of drafts a week. The feature is off and not wired today, but this is its core input.
findings.recommendation: Use absolute, factual buckets for the label ('bought once', '2-3 orders', '4+'), not terciles. Show the judge the label and require honesty against it. Forbid copy that asserts purchase history unless the type is homogeneous on that trait (check member spread, not only the median).

findings.assumption: 'Every number comes from code': claims.check_numbers guarantees a briefing (and the Scientist Judge's explanation) never carries a wrong number.
findings.problem: The check matches only magnitudes against any value in the dict. The sign is ignored by design, and names are ignored. So a loss of ₹12,400 written as 'made ₹12,400 extra profit' passes. 'Confident it earned ₹31,000', which is the absolute value of the low bound, passes. '5,200 of 8,000 customers bought', using the sent count, passes. The headline is checked against every section's numbers pooled together. Indian formatting (₹1,24,000, ₹1.2 lakh) is always flagged, so Indian-style briefings fall back to the template, which is safe but means the LLM text is mostly unused in India.
findings.evidence: autonomy/agents/claims.py:11 ('Signs are ignored') and 55 (abs(value)); autonomy/agents/analyst.py:558 and 567 (headline vs pooled 'every'). Probe: check_numbers(...) returned [] for 'The agent made ₹12,400 extra profit, likely between ₹6,200 and ₹31,000.' with profit=-12400, low=-31000, high=6200; returned [] for 'We are confident it earned ₹31,000…' and for '5,200 of 8,000 customers bought' (sent=5200); and flagged '₹1','24,000' for '₹1,24,000'.
findings.real_world_impact: v2 already overestimated value about 10x (REAL_DATA_RESULTS). An LLM that flips the direction in the one sentence the marketer with 30 minutes a week reads would make them keep paying for a losing agent. The 300k CRM team could take a 'confident' headline built from a bound to leadership.
findings.recommendation: Bind numbers to names. Have the model reference placeholders ({profit}, {low}) that code fills in, or require that each number used comes with the direction word code computed. Check the headline only against a whitelisted set, and add lakh and crore parsing.

findings.assumption: The Data Doctor chat's 'number check' (a number in a reply must be in a tool result) prevents made-up statistics.
findings.problem: Grounding is lexical: any equal number anywhere in the evidence grounds a claim with a different meaning. A null rate of 0.12 grounds '12% of your customers will churn next month'. columns_total=14 grounds 'Your churn is 14%' and '₹14 lakh'. Words ('about half', 'twelve percent') are not checked at all. This is the one LLM that is live in production, and it reads every client's uploaded data.
findings.evidence: engine/agent/grounding.py:1-20 and ungrounded_numbers. Probe with evidence {rows: 8000, null_rate: 0.12, columns_total: 14, repeat_buyers: 2310}: ungrounded_numbers returned [] for '12% of your customers will churn next month', 'Your churn is 14%', '2310 customers are your VIPs, worth ₹14 lakh', 'About half of your 8,000 customers churned' and 'Revenue grew twelve percent'.
findings.real_world_impact: A shop uploading 14 months of Shopify orders can be told a confident, made-up churn or revenue figure that passes the guardrail and is shown as checked. That figure then anchors the goals they set.
findings.recommendation: Treat the number check as a weak filter and say so in the docs. For statistics, make replies cite an evidence id per number (number plus source key) and verify the pairing, and flag spelled-out quantities. Add a real-model red-team set of 'semantic swap' cases to the Doctor evals.

findings.assumption: Opt-outs are honoured at once by a hard keyword net, so no classifier can miss a STOP (conversation.py docstring).
findings.problem: The net is English plus a few European words. For an India-first WhatsApp product it misses common opt-outs: 'band karo', 'mat bhejo', 'message mat karo', 'बंद करो', 'मैसेज मत भेजो', 'nahi chahiye', 'pls dont msg me', 'dnd', 'not interested'. With the default PersonReadsReplies these only raise a reply.needs_human alert, and the customer is not held, so the agent keeps messaging until someone reads the inbox. With LLMTextSignals, the model's self-reported 'probability' at or above 0.6 for 'other' or 'not_now' means no human sees it. 'not_now' snoozes for 30 days instead of unsubscribing. One injected reply in a batch of 20 can also steer the others' labels.
findings.evidence: Probe: stop_keyword() returned None for every Hindi/Hinglish phrase above; 'Stop karo' and 'unsubscribe karo' matched only because they contain English words. autonomy/agents/conversation.py:45-81 (keyword lists) and 236-239 (needs_human only when confidence < 0.6); autonomy/runtime/service.py:1572-1580 (needs_human only raises an alert, no hold); autonomy/signals/llm_signals.py:20-25 (batch of 20, self-reported probability used as confidence).
findings.real_world_impact: An Indian WhatsApp customer writes 'band karo' and keeps receiving marketing templates. That leads to block and report actions, a falling quality rating, and a paused or banned number (the failure DECISIONS V-1 calls irreversible), plus TRAI/DPDP exposure.
findings.recommendation: Add Hindi, Hinglish and regional opt-out lexicons (Devanagari and romanised) to the hard net. Put a contact hold on any customer with an unreviewed reply until it is resolved. Never trust LLM self-reported probability as calibration: calibrate on labelled replies, or route every non-keyword reply to a person or a hold. Classify one reply per call, or isolate replies per call.

findings.assumption: AI writes 5-10 drafts per type, a scoring model picks, and live tests cut losers, which fixes the plan's own lesson that 'raw LLM subject lines lost; AI writing needs a scoring model in front of it' (plan-v3.md:55, 270-290).
findings.problem: At the target sizes neither safeguard can switch on. Types are refitted weekly and the LiveBoard is not persisted, so each live test lasts one week. At 8k customers there are 300 types of about 27 customers, about 9 customers per live draft per week, against the 300 sends per arm needed to cut. Even if everyone were messaged weekly that is about 34 weeks, and the test resets every week. The scoring model's gate (at least 200 training purchases over draft-by-type cells) fails, so ranking falls back to theme labels. Raw LLM drafts go live: the exact configuration the plan cites as losing.
findings.evidence: autonomy/content/types.py:200-201 (type count); docs/v3/COPY.md 'Open: persisting the fitted types and the board' and 'Type ids are only meaningful within a week'. Arithmetic with CopyConfig defaults: 8,000 customers gives 300 types, 27 per type, 9 per live draft per week, 33.8 weeks to 300 sends per arm, and 2,400 drafts plus 4,800 judge calls a week. 50,000 gives 56 per draft per week and 5.4 weeks. 300,000 gives 333 per draft per week and 0.9 weeks. COPY.md's only evidence is a planted synthetic signal (6 types x 40 drafts x 2,000 sends).
findings.real_world_impact: The 8k shop pays for 2,400 drafts and 4,800 judge calls per goal per week, and gets unscored LLM copy that is never eliminated. Only the 300k shop that messages everyone weekly could ever cut a draft, and then only within one week's types.
findings.recommendation: Size types to the data (for example k is at most purchases per week divided by a minimum, often under 10 for small shops), persist types and boards across weeks, and pool drafts across weeks by content features. Below a size threshold, do not run per-type LLM copy: use a small, human-reviewed library. Make 'scoring model trusted' a precondition for live per-type copy, not a fallback.

findings.assumption: Per-type copy works on WhatsApp once templates are 'submitted as a weekly batch' (COPY.md Open), and the Critic gates what WhatsApp customers see.
findings.problem: No code submits or syncs WhatsApp templates with Meta. Sending posts only the template name and parameters, so the text a customer sees is whatever Meta holds under that name, not the body the Critic approved. Nothing checks that the two match. Per-type copy makes up to 2,400 new template names per goal per week (a name is never reused). That is far above what a WhatsApp Business account can hold or get approved. Meta's per-account template limits are a few hundred unverified and a few thousand verified; this is from Meta's public docs, not checked in this repo.
findings.evidence: autonomy/channels/whatsapp.py:137-163 (payload is template name, language and params only); grep for 'message_templates|submit_template' across autonomy/api/engine found nothing; autonomy/agents/creative.py template_name() is unique per type and week; docs/v3/COPY.md 'Open: … WhatsApp templates need Meta's approval'.
findings.real_world_impact: For the India-first WhatsApp shop, decision 6 cannot work on its main channel. Sends to unsubmitted names fail at Meta, and a hand-made template with the same name but different wording bypasses the Critic entirely.
findings.recommendation: Keep WhatsApp on a small, human-approved, Meta-synced template set (fetch approved template bodies and run the Critic on them). Allow per-type variation only through parameters within approved templates, and add a send-time check that the Meta-approved body equals the Critic-approved body.

findings.assumption: The Strategist's weekly adjustment is safe because it 'may only narrow' the plan inside the envelope (strategist.py docstring; orchestrator brief_within).
findings.problem: Narrowing is applied whenever the LLM asks, with no check that the evidence supports it. BriefAdjustment requires the model to list keep_channels and keep_offer_ids, so leaving a channel out by mistake removes it. Narrowing only ratchets: re-widening needs a new marketer-approved brief. With mid-market sample sizes, nearly every weekly section reads 'not clear yet', so the LLM is in effect acting on noise and can drop WhatsApp or the best offer permanently.
findings.evidence: autonomy/agents/strategist.py:158-169 (keep lists), 387-418 (adjust_brief applies _narrow; the only number check is on the rationale text), 559-599 (_narrow drops anything not listed; refuses only dropping every channel or offer); the docstring says re-widening needs marketer approval.
findings.real_world_impact: The 30-minutes-a-week marketer may not notice that WhatsApp silently left the plan in week 2. Per the plan, offer and channel choice is where the money is, so the agent narrows itself out of it. This is wired whenever the runtime gets a Strategist (demo today).
findings.recommendation: Let code gate narrowing: drop a channel or offer only when its interval is clearly below the alternatives over enough sends, and treat an omission as 'keep'. Expire narrowings automatically after N weeks or surface them as one-click undo in the inbox.

findings.assumption: v3 STATUS and plan-v3 describe what was built (meta-risk the user raised).
findings.problem: Several confident claims go beyond what the code does. (a) STATUS.md marks decisions 5, 6, 8 and the experiments as 'Built' with no 'not wired' column, yet COPY.md says 'Nothing in the loop calls it yet'. ExperimentBook.start is called only from the Gym runner, so no experiment self-starts in production. Approved image banners are 'stored but not sent', with no raster output and no scheduler. The early-signal and auto-budget weekly job 'is not written'. build_from_order_log is called by no tool. (b) plan-v3.md:74 says the new AI steps 'all go through' engine/llm_http.py 'each with its own allowance', but no autonomy module imports llm_http and there is no per-role allowance. (c) plan-v3.md:277 promises a judge 'from a different model family (unchanged)', but samples.py uses one model for both. (d) plan-v3.md:276 promises refill-date and points slots, which are not done. (e) The CI 'proof' runs (agent_v3 in the Gym and real bench) contain no LLM piece, so no CI result can confirm any AI-writing or vision claim. (f) In the v2 Scientist evidence, 5 of 15 'real model answers' were first written by the grading agent itself (later replaced).
findings.evidence: docs/v3/STATUS.md:12-29; docs/v3/COPY.md:5; autonomy/experiments/gymrun.py:228 is the only ExperimentBook.start call (grep); docs/v3/IMAGES.md:127-128 and 156-166; docs/v3/PRESET.md 'Not switched on by AUTONOMY_V3' (early signals, copy, images); grep build_from_order_log finds only its definition in engine/doctor/order_log_workflow.py; grep 'llm_http' in autonomy/ finds nothing; autonomy/brand/samples.py:266-271; docs/v2/SCIENTIST.md:79-84.
findings.real_world_impact: A founder or investor reading STATUS would believe v3 runs live experiments, writes per-type copy and moves budget. A pilot shop would see none of it, and the planned proof runs cannot show otherwise.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Wired into production? / Exercised by a real model? / Measured on real data?' column to STATUS for every row. Strike or qualify the plan lines above. Keep the 'what was run' tables (they are good) and add a 'what calls this' line to each doc.

findings.assumption: The vision checker meets the plan's 'catches at least 95% of planted bad images' bar.
findings.problem: The only model-side checker is a fake that reads flags the fake provider wrote into the PNG. The 95% test is 100% by construction, which IMAGES.md honestly says. No real vision model has been evaluated for 'right product', 'logo intact' or 'garbled text', which are exactly the tasks VLMs are unreliable at. Missing logo notes default to 'ok'. Digits use western grouping, not lakh style, for an India-first product.
findings.evidence: tests/v3/images/test_check.py:201-214 (docstring: '100% by construction'); autonomy/assets/check.py:252-267 (observe_fake_png reads PNG text notes; NOTE_LOGO default 'ok'); docs/v3/IMAGES.md:166-176 and 186-187.
findings.real_world_impact: None today, since banners are never sent. When a real model is plugged in, the 95% figure will not carry over, and a wrong-product or broken-logo banner can reach batch approval, where a busy marketer approves 20 at once.
findings.recommendation: Do not mark the decision-5 bar as met. Build a real-image eval set (real catalogue photos and real model outputs with human labels), measure per-reason recall and precision with the chosen VLM, and gate enabling on that.

findings.assumption: Template copy and the demo show what honest, Critic-approved copy looks like.
findings.problem: TEMPLATE_COPY, which is what production actually sends (see C1), makes claims nothing verifies. NOVELTY: 'there is something new in {{top_category}}', with no check for new products. SOCIAL_PROOF: 'a favourite with shoppers like you'. It is approved on rules alone. The API demo hardcodes a Critic verdict 'judge: brand voice 5, honesty 5', 'approved' on invented-scarcity copy ('a few {{top_category}} picks are almost gone'): a judge result no model produced, on copy the rubric says to reject.
findings.evidence: autonomy/agents/creative.py TEMPLATE_COPY (NOVELTY and SOCIAL_PROOF entries, around lines 161-220); api/v2/deps.py:1057-1068.
findings.real_world_impact: Shops send small but false claims ('something new' when nothing is new). Demo viewers see a fabricated approval of dishonest copy presented as the editor's output.
findings.recommendation: Make template claims conditional on data (novelty only when the catalogue has items added in the last N days). Remove the hardcoded verdict, or run the real rules on the demo draft and show their actual result.

findings.assumption: Judging each item twice with the rubric order reversed reduces bias.
findings.problem: Both runs use the same model at temperature 0 with near-identical prompts, so they are highly correlated. This doubles judge cost (4,800 calls per goal-week for per-type copy) for little independence. The Creative also latches 'down' after one failed call for the rest of a weekly run, so one transient error sends all remaining types to template copy (only noted, not alerted).
findings.evidence: autonomy/agents/critic.py:440-480 (two ask_json runs, temperature default 0.0 in autonomy/agents/base.py:52-60); autonomy/agents/creative.py:530-537 (reset docstring: 'a model that went down stays skipped').
findings.real_world_impact: Higher LLM spend for no measured gain. A per-type copy week can silently degrade to templates.
findings.recommendation: Use one judge call with a second model family, or self-consistency at temperature above 0 measured on an eval. Retry transient errors per cell, and raise an alert when more than X% of cells are templated.

verdicts.reasoning: The core claim holds for the v2/v3 marketing agent. api/v2/app.py:153 and 163-166 build BrandServices with no llm (the field defaults to None at api/v2/onboarding_brand.py:70), so goal_library falls back to _NoModel (autonomy/brand/samples.py:95-99, 264-271). The production build_runtime call (api/v2/app.py:202, and also autonomy/runtime/service.py:3313) passes no analyst, strategist or text_signals. The weekly cycle returns early when either is None (service.py:2965-2966). Replies default to PersonReadsReplies (service.py:1165), and get_judge_llm returns None (api/v2/engines/studio.py:551-553). RuntimeSettings has no LLM fields at all. Only autonomy/runtime/demo.py:2083-2102 wires an analyst and strategist. Two parts are overstated. (1) 'The only live LLM in production is the v1 Data Doctor' is false: the v1 API also runs LLM campaign copy, root-cause summaries and a RAG assistant (api/routes/generative.py header, Meter(... llm=generative.llm) at :682). (2) The fallback is not hidden in code: the samples.py:259 docstring says 'with no model configured the rules are the judge', and docs/v3/STATUS.md does not claim LLMs are live. I could not confirm the claim that the marketer is told an AI writes the copy. The system works, but as rule-checked template copy. The finding is a gap between capability and claim that also means no LLM can be configured for the agent at all, so major, not blocker.

I re-ran the probe and got the same result: check_rules returns [] for 7 of 8 dishonest bodies, and only 'Rs. 500 off' is caught by _MONEY_BEFORE (critic.py:127-128). With a raising judge and judge_optional=True, all 7 come back 'approved on the rules alone (judge optional)' (critic.py:454-457 latch, 504-507). The same model and model_id go to both the Creative and the Critic (samples.py:266-271). That contradicts plan-v3.md:277 ('a judge from a different model family') and the critic.py:19 docstring. judge_optional is set only in samples.py:269. The v3 CopyPlanner takes a separate Critic and rules and does not set it. The harmful path is overstated for production today: per C1, no LLM can be configured, so every draft is TEMPLATE_COPY, which is fixed text. A judge outage therefore approves only template copy. The scenario needs an LLM wired for the Creative, LLM drafts written, and then the judge failing partway through the review. All of this is latent, but it becomes a real hole the moment an LLM is wired. The regex gaps in the discount and scarcity rules are real regardless.

autonomy/content/types.py:316-318 returns words[1] when low >= high. q_lo and q_hi are terciles of the base (types.py:339-340), and the purchases label uses ('few orders','repeat buyer','frequent buyer') (:357-361). I re-ran types_probe.py: 75 types, with 1047 of 1047 one-time buyers in types labelled 'repeat buyer'. For example, ct000 'lapsed, repeat buyer, mid spend…' has 89 members, all with 1 purchase. The label is all the writer sees (CustomerType.note returns label, types.py:190-193). One partial mitigation: the judge's honesty criterion asks whether every claim is 'supportable from what is given here' (critic.py:~115), so a real judge might reject 'thanks for coming back' as unsupported. That depends on the LLM judge being live, which it is not (C1). The planner is not wired ('Nothing in the loop calls it yet', docs/v3/COPY.md:5), so the impact is latent. It is still the feature's core input, and it is wrong for typical D2C data.

autonomy/agents/claims.py:11-12 says 'Signs are ignored' by design, and _reads_as compares to abs(value) (:55). The check_numbers docstring says the names are not used. I re-ran the probe: check_numbers('The agent made ₹12,400 extra profit, likely between ₹6,200 and ₹31,000.', {profit:-12400, low:-31000, high:6200}) returned []. '₹1,24,000 or ₹1.2 lakh' returned ['₹1','24,000','₹1.2'], so Indian formats are always flagged. analyst.py:558-567 checks the headline against the pooled 'every' dict. The direction words (analyst.py:186-205, _verdict) are only instructions in the prompt notes, and nothing verifies that the text keeps them. Impact today is latent because analyst=None in production (C1), so briefings come from code. The 'every number comes from code' guarantee is still weaker than described, and the 10x overestimate history makes a sign flip a serious failure once the LLM is wired.

The mechanism is confirmed. I re-ran it with grounded_numbers([{rows:8000, null_rate:0.12, columns_total:14, repeat_buyers:2310}]): ungrounded_numbers returned [] for '12% of your customers will churn next month', 'Your churn is 14%', '…worth ₹14 lakh', 'About half of your 8,000…' and 'twelve percent'. 'Churn is 37%' was flagged. The check is used live in engine/agent/loop.py:390 and engine/doctor/protocol.py:552. The framing is overstated, though. The module docstring (engine/agent/grounding.py:1-5) openly calls this an arithmetic presence check ('the check is arithmetic, not a judge'). It is one of two checks: guardrails follow at loop.py:391. It does not claim to verify meaning. Lexical number grounding is a known weak filter. The added risk is a semantic swap, which needs the model to reuse an evidence number with a new meaning. That is plausible but unmeasured, and I could not confirm that the UI labels such replies 'checked'. Treat it as a documentation and defence-in-depth gap rather than a broken guarantee.

Confirmed: STOP_EXACT and STOP_PATTERNS (autonomy/agents/conversation.py:43-81) are English plus arret/baja/parar/alto/stopp. My probe: stop_keyword returned None for 'band karo', 'mat bhejo', 'बंद करो', 'nahi chahiye', 'dnd', 'not interested' and 'pls dont msg me'. 'Stop karo' matched only through 'stop'. needs_human only raises an alert (service.py:1572-1580). I found no contact hold for a customer with an unreviewed reply anywhere in autonomy/ (grep for needs_human hits only service.py:1572). One mitigation the finding misses: WhatsApp's own marketing opt-out is honoured. Meta failure code 131050 ('stopped marketing messages from this business') is turned into a BLOCK that withdraws consent (autonomy/channels/whatsapp.py:51-53, 293-294). Quick-reply button payloads are also parsed (:356-368). So a customer who uses WhatsApp's built-in stop control is protected, and the gap is free-text Hinglish or Hindi opt-outs. The LLMTextSignals self-reported-confidence and batch-injection points are latent, because no production path configures text_signals (C1). For an India-first product that misses common free-text opt-outs and keeps sending until a person reads the inbox, major is right. Blocker would be too strong given the 131050 path and the alert.

choose_k (types.py:196-201) with CopyConfig defaults (autonomy/content/config.py: min_types 50, max_types 300, members_per_type 20, drafts_per_type 8, top_k 3, min_sends_per_arm 300, min_train_purchases 200) gives 8000//20=400, capped to 300 types of about 27 members each. That is 3 live drafts per type, so about 9 sends per draft per week at most. 2,400 drafts per goal-week, plus two judge runs each (critic.py rubric_orders), gives 4,800 judge calls. planner.py:223 creates a fresh LiveBoard(cfg) every run, and COPY.md:34 and :171 confirm that types are refitted weekly and that persistence is open. So no draft can reach 300 sends per arm before the board resets at 8k. Even at 50k it takes about 5 weeks against a 1-week board. When the scoring model is not trusted, ranking falls back to theme-label rate (planner.py:11-12), and the top_k still go live. The planner is not wired yet (COPY.md:5), so the cost is not incurred today. The arithmetic and the design conclusion hold.

Confirmed, and broader than stated. WhatsAppAdapter.build_payload (autonomy/channels/whatsapp.py:137-163) sends only template name, language and params, plus an optional header image. A grep for message_templates or submit_template across autonomy, api and engine finds nothing, so no code creates, submits or syncs templates with Meta, and nothing compares Meta's approved body to the Critic-approved body. The name comes from creative.template_name (creative.py:416-434), which is unique per goal, brief version, channel, offer, theme and index (plus type for v3). The dispatcher passes item.template_name straight through (dispatcher.py:385). This already applies to v2's zero-touch library: template_strategist starts briefs on email plus WhatsApp, and goal_library writes WhatsApp items with these generated names. So on the live production path, every WhatsApp send targets a name Meta has never approved, unless someone hand-creates each one, and every brief version bump renames them. It fails safe: Meta rejects the send, and the wrong text is not delivered. But the India-first main channel cannot work as built, which meets the blocker definition. The 'same-name hand template bypasses the Critic' path is real but needs manual action. The Meta limit numbers are external and not checked in this repo.

BriefAdjustment requires the lists keep_channels and keep_offer_ids (strategist.py:158-169). _narrow (:559-599) keeps only the listed channels and offers, so an omitted channel is dropped. It refuses only an empty channel list or empty offer list, and NO_OFFER is always kept. adjust_brief (:387-418) applies the narrowing with no evidence gate. The only check on the output is that the rationale's numbers are in the report. Narrowing is against the current brief.envelope, so a channel outside it is 'ignored', and the docstring at :33 says 're-widening needs the marketer to approve a new brief'. This confirms the ratchet. Wiring: the weekly cycle runs only when both analyst and strategist are set (service.py:2965-2966), and that happens only in autonomy/runtime/demo.py:2083-2084, not in production. Latent today, but the design flaw is real and acts on noise at mid-market sample sizes.

Holds, and the gap is wider than stated. autonomy/runtime/agent.py:2859-2860 stores _offer_goal[(customer, d.action.offer_id)], and 2865-2868 looks it up by e.attrs['offer_id']. autonomy/connectors/shopify/mapping.py:138,151 sets offer_id = codes[0], the raw discount code. OfferOption (autonomy/contracts/goals.py:77-115) has no code or prefix field. The hand-off can carry a per-person code (autonomy/channels/klaviyo.py:175,201), but nothing passes discount_code=; grep finds no caller, and docs/v2/CONNECTORS.md:405 admits it. CREATE_DISCOUNT is only defined in the connector, with no runtime caller. BudgetPrice.update (autonomy/decide/pacing.py:431-434) with spent_today=0 gives miss=-1, so the price decays to the floor and price returns 0 (pacing.py:410-414). New point: the v2 mandate money rule, SpendLedger (service.py:659-668, 813-819), matches on the same attrs offer_id == brief offer_id, so it also misses real Shopify redemptions. The 'separate money rule' does not save it. Only workaround: name OfferOption.offer_id exactly as a shared Shopify code (e.g. offer_id='COMEBACK10'). That is undocumented, case-sensitive, and breaks per-person codes. On real Shopify orders the claim of offer budget control is false.

The core holds. service.py:3044-3054 keys the policy cache on (material_brief, approved content ids), and MATERIAL_BRIEF_FIELDS (service.py:303-305) includes the whole envelope. Any budget change, offer change or content approval rebuilds the policy, and a restart empties _policies. LOOKALIKE.md:72-77 admits the crowd starts empty after every rebuild. The replay runs before _decided, and the lookalike observe at agent.py:2808 requires _decided. PRESET.md:105 admits the ExperimentBook is not persisted. who.py:342-346 and 404-414: _frozen is rebuilt from scratch, and load counts only SEND events (who.py:418-420). Customers held back have low load and are re-keyed 'light', which is the oscillation the docstring warns about. Mis-described part: BudgetPrice does not simply 'forget what was spent'. The replay calls _keep -> _price_send for every replayed decision (agent.py:2940-2941), so replay_lookback (30 days, service.py:355) of channel spend lands in _channel_spend. The first roll after the first decision (agent.py:2824, 2890) then closes it as ONE day. Probe: BudgetPrice(30000,30).update(6000, other_spend=12000) gives remaining=0, exhausted=True, price=ceiling 1000, still exhausted 5 days later. A steady run with the same spend gives price 0.06. So when a month of channel spend is more than about budget/30 (e.g. WhatsApp at a realistic per-message cost), every rebuild prices offers at the ceiling for about 2 weeks. With email at 0.001 it is harmless. Either way, the offer price after a rebuild is wrong. A weekly creative approval means the lookalike crowd never fills its windows.

Mechanism confirmed. WhoBook.ingest (autonomy/decide/who.py:351-359) keeps every event with no type filter, and who.py has no pruning. By contrast, the agent's own _events is pruned to the learn horizon (agent.py:3050-3060), and its pre-decision history keeps only _HISTORY_KEEP types (agent.py:2730-2740). So the who book defeats the 'compact digest' design. _feed_history passes every customer's full history (service.py:2829-2857). My probe: about 1,701 bytes per pydantic Event. Overstated parts: (a) the Klaviyo ENGAGEMENT backfill is 180 days, not 14 months (autonomy/connectors/klaviyo/connector.py:163-168), so the 8k brand starts nearer 8k x ~90-100 events, i.e. 1.2-1.4 GB per goal rather than 3.4 GB, though it then grows without bound. (b) The production API does not tick (allow_tick defaults False, api/v2/deps.py:197,456; app.py:214 does not pass it), so there is no second copy there. (c) who.refresh refits the slow models only when a new month-end window has closed (who.py:371-377), not on every sweep, but always after a rebuild. At the stated target of 50k-5M customers, raw event retention per goal is multiple to tens of GB, and a slow fit inside decide blocks the single sequential worker (worker.py:579-586). Blocker for the target market; marginal for the 8k shop.

There are no imports of autonomy.content outside the package; the only hit is a docstring in autonomy/agents/creative.py:429. Nothing outside tests calls ImageServices(. The only book.start is in autonomy/experiments/gymrun.py:228. Nothing in autonomy/runtime or api references early_signal or auto-budget. api/v2/engines/doctor.py:1386-1430 returns MapEventsResponse(events=...) and never appends. autonomy/bridges/doctor_bridge.map_file has no caller outside tests. The writes into the EventStore are only connectors, webhooks (deps.py:640-652, 3363), the dispatcher and the demo. api/v2/onboarding.py and autonomy/onboarding have no event import. In code the slow models are autonomy/decide/slow_models.py on agent events, not the order-log rows. A non-Shopify or CSV-only shop cannot start the agent.

Partly true. tick_handler queues the successor before tick(now) (worker.py:266-272). JobQueue.claim has no lease on RUNNING ticks (store/queue.py:55-80). There is no advisory lock anywhere in autonomy/runtime or autonomy/store. RuntimeCursor is created fresh (service.py:1170; build_worker passes none, 3313-3318), so a restart reruns nightly, weekly and today's sweep (the docstring at 428-432 says repeats are no-ops by decision id). With two workers, overlap and split brains are real. Refuted part: the production API cannot run POST /v2/runtime/tick. allow_tick defaults False (api/v2/deps.py:197) and raises Forbidden (deps.py:456-457); app.py:214 does not set it, and only the demo does (deps.py:1561). So there is no 'separate cold brain' deciding in production. The code assumes one worker ('the one worker claims them', settings.py:485), and one sequential worker cannot overlap itself. The risk only appears if an operator scales workers, which is a missing guard and doc, not a normal-use failure. Minor, or major only for a 300k shop that scales out.

The stated mechanism is mostly wrong, but the real problem is worse. The Klaviyo mapping does map opens and clicks with no bot or Apple Mail Privacy Protection filter (klaviyo/mapping.py:56-59; grep finds nothing). But the rate features divide by SEND counts (profile/features.py:403-404, 409; facts.py:323-331), and Klaviyo history arrives as DELIVER, OPEN and CLICK, never SEND (no connector emits EventType.SEND). Probe: 20 weekly DELIVER+OPEN and 7 CLICKs 2 s after delivery give ch_open_rate=0, ch_click_rate=0, ch_email_engage_rate=0, ch_engaged=1. So inflated opens cannot reach the rates, and the trait key does not use opens (who.py:125-133); opens are also labelled 'weak' in features.py:413-415. What actually happens: for imported history every rate feature is 0, so who's click cut is the median of zeros and the 'answers_more' group is empty. ch_engaged = 'ever clicked' is what scanner clicks inflate, which sorts customers into 'answers_less' instead of 'silent'. Look-alike and tiredness models read the same dead features. Engagement traits do not describe real behaviour, for a different reason than claimed.

configs/v3/journeys.yaml:36-44 sets value_bar: 50. journeys.py:443 compares it to first.value_if_converted, which is the value model's order value in the shop's currency (bidders.py:1717). with_value_bar has no caller. calendar_in.yaml:17 lists only 2026 and 2027. One mitigation: the bar is only a pre-filter. A journey bid still competes in the auction on net value, so 'offered to nearly everyone' is a bit strong. But the net subtracts DEFAULT_CHANNEL_COSTS WHATSAPP=0.03 'in the goal's currency' (bidders.py:150-160), about ₹0.03 against a real ~₹0.8+ marketing conversation, and runtime settings expose no per-channel cost override. So for a rupee shop both the bar and the WhatsApp cost are in dollar-scale units, and WhatsApp-first journeys pass easily. The calendar gap is minor today (2028 is 14 months away) but fails silently.

Probe: RuntimeSettings has 46 fields, RuntimeConfig 30, LookalikeConfig 17, WhoConfig 12, matching the finding. settings.py:384 builds extra={'lookalike': True} only when the flag is set. With v3 on, resolve_v3 (v3.py:126) treats lookalike=None as the preset's True, so AUTONOMY_LOOKALIKE_MODEL=false is ignored. PRESET.md:87 confirms urgency up to 3.75. The sign is preserved (it scales net, so a losing message stays losing), but it multiplies an already overestimated value. PRESET.md:48 admits the decisions explain engine ignores the setting. STATUS.md:31-34: no Gym or real-bench comparison yet. V3Preset can toggle parts in code, but production has only the all-or-nothing switch. This is a fair judgement-level major.
